techniques.name: Full House
techniques.description: A row, column or box has one empty cell left; it gets the missing digit.

techniques.name: Hidden Single
techniques.description: A digit has only one possible cell in a row, column or box.

techniques.name: Naked Single
techniques.description: A cell has only one candidate left.

techniques.name: Pointing Pair/Triple
techniques.description: Inside a box a digit is confined to one row or column, so it leaves the rest of that line.

techniques.name: Box/Line Reduction
techniques.description: Inside a row or column a digit is confined to one box, so it leaves the rest of that box.

techniques.name: Naked Pair
techniques.description: Two cells in a unit share the same two candidates; those digits leave the rest of the unit.

techniques.name: Hidden Pair
techniques.description: Two digits can only go in the same two cells of a unit; other candidates leave those cells.

techniques.name: Naked Triple
techniques.description: Three cells in a unit hold only three digits between them; those digits leave the rest of the unit.

techniques.name: Hidden Triple
techniques.description: Three digits can only go in the same three cells of a unit; other candidates leave those cells.

techniques.name: X-Wing
techniques.description: In two rows a digit fits only the same two columns (or vice versa); it leaves the rest of those columns.

techniques.name: Skyscraper
techniques.description: Two conjugate pairs in parallel lines share one end line; a cell seeing both other ends loses the digit.

techniques.name: Two-String Kite
techniques.description: A row conjugate pair and a column conjugate pair meet in a box; a cell seeing both far ends loses the digit.

techniques.name: XY-Wing
techniques.description: A bivalue pivot {x,y} sees pincers {x,z} and {y,z}; cells seeing both pincers lose z.

techniques.name: XYZ-Wing
techniques.description: A pivot {x,y,z} sees pincers {x,z} and {y,z}; cells seeing all three lose z.

techniques.name: Simple Colouring
techniques.description: Colour chains of conjugate pairs of one digit in two colours; exactly one colour is true.

techniques.name: Swordfish
techniques.description: In three rows a digit fits only the same three columns (or vice versa); it leaves the rest of those columns.

techniques.name: Naked Quad
techniques.description: Four cells in a unit hold only four digits between them; those digits leave the rest of the unit.

techniques.name: Hidden Quad
techniques.description: Four digits can only go in the same four cells of a unit; other candidates leave those cells.

techniques.name: Turbot Fish
techniques.description: Strong link, weak link, strong link on one digit; a cell seeing both ends loses the digit.

techniques.name: W-Wing
techniques.description: Two identical bivalue cells {x,y} joined by a conjugate pair on x; cells seeing both lose y.

techniques.name: Unique Rectangle Type 1
techniques.description: Three corners of a two-box rectangle are exactly {a,b}; the fourth corner cannot be a or b.

techniques.name: Unique Rectangle Type 2
techniques.description: Two corners are {a,b} and the other two are {a,b,x}; cells seeing both x corners lose x.

techniques.name: Unique Rectangle Type 4
techniques.description: Two corners are {a,b}; if a is locked to the other two corners in a unit, those corners lose b.

techniques.name: BUG+1
techniques.description: All empty cells are bivalue except one; that cell takes the digit that appears three times in its units.

techniques.name: Finned X-Wing
techniques.description: An X-Wing with extra candidates (fins) in one box; cells in the cover lines that see the fins lose the digit.

techniques.name: Jellyfish
techniques.description: In four rows a digit fits only the same four columns (or vice versa).

techniques.name: Finned Swordfish
techniques.description: A Swordfish with fins in one box; cells in the cover lines that see the fins lose the digit.

techniques.name: X-Chain
techniques.description: An alternating chain of strong and weak links on one digit; cells seeing both ends lose the digit.

techniques.name: XY-Chain
techniques.description: A chain of bivalue cells, each linked to the next by a shared digit; cells seeing both ends lose the end digit.

techniques.name: Alternating Inference Chain
techniques.description: A chain mixing bivalue cells and conjugate pairs across digits; candidates that conflict with both ends are removed.

techniques.name: ALS-XZ
techniques.description: Two almost locked sets share a restricted common digit X; a common digit Z leaves cells seeing all its copies.

techniques.name: Sue de Coq
techniques.description: Cells at a box/line intersection plus cells from the line and box lock their digits into the line or box.

techniques.name: Forcing Chain
techniques.description: Try every candidate of a cell (or every place for a digit in a unit); if all lead to the same result, it is true.
